reviews.text: I've been testing this game since beta - i'll try to share the pros and cons objectively: Pros: - the game design is quite good. you currently have two disciplines available with different build options and can achieve a lot of different specs with your castle management. - replayability is quite satisfactory. there are different bosses and you will not be bored with different builds (a lot of skills and items to choose from) - the lore is quite detailed. if you like vampires it's a pro for you. Cons: - it's early access. there were a lot of bugs while i started testing but could not find any major ones in the last few days. - the game needs a bit more polishing with its animations and UI. Overall, the game is quite promising and I'd recommend it.

Few Nights More - I'm a big fan of games such as Slay the spire. Seeing this, with it's atmosphere, universe, and detail i was intrigued. I'm someone who is quite weary of Early Access titles, sometimes they just get overlooked and forgotten. Upon checking this games discord, the dev team are active, listening and helpful. I took the plunge. Firstly it's irritatingly addictive, my attention span is lacking borderline non existent, but i found myself wanting to run one more run, one more night, one more death. each time. The gameplay is simple, yet complex, the growth of the character feels good, and is interesting, the castle system, with rooms, decor, traps and minions are overwhelming at the start but soon i wrapped my head around the systems, and found them rewarding and enjoyable, the prestige system is good and has me evaluating each option. After a run, you get rewarded with points to further improve lineages, castles and other options, the more you play the more you're rewarded, and honestly its addictive. That said it is Early access, so some animations aren't the most detailed, some music loops and becomes tiresome. The Dev team are active, and inspire me with confidence their work is a passion, and they're moving forward with it listening to the userbase. This could be the next big thing, If the style of gameplay interests you, i'd heavily reccomend buying. the amount of content already is superb. with only more to come.

[h1] 游戏背景[/h1] 吸血鬼作为星球最早存在的生物也是星球的统治种族，在一场战争中几乎被毁灭，现在，是时候复仇，重建家园，并夺回属于吸血鬼的一切了。 [h1] 回合制战斗+地牢建设[/h1] 作为一名吸血鬼领主，本作自然也就是所谓的反向地下城，玩家要通过房间、房间装饰、陷阱和仆从的布置，对来犯的敌人进行阻碍，并击败敌人。 一开始我以为游戏会是类似《地牢制造者/dungeon maker》这样地牢房间+怪物布置完成后全自动战斗的游戏。而游玩之后，就个人短暂的游戏体验而言，本作最主要的游戏要素还是回合制战斗，而非地牢建设。 游戏中的房间、装饰多半用于辅助角色，陷阱与怪物效果基本都是对敌人进行轻微削弱，最后敌人都需要玩家进行战斗来解决。 [h1] rogue类型[/h1] 作为一款肉鸽游戏，死亡即从头来过，所以本作自然不是经营类型的地牢游戏，在死亡后结算本局成绩，获得一定的点数，可用来解锁更多的角色、地图，或者提升初始的属性、技能效果。 游戏的随机因素在于属性、技能、房间、饰品、怪物、商人等多个方面。每轮都能获得不同的提升。 [h1] 游戏内容[/h1] 每轮游戏从选择角色开始，之后选择地图与地形。地图主要是初始技能的不同，地形则决定游戏开始时，空房间的数量与位置。 本作一共有8个吸血鬼角色可以选择，每个角色具有3条正面效果和1个负面效果以及1个主动技能，彼此词条各不相同的。 在布置完成后，即可进入战斗，每个夜晚多名敌人进入玩家的地下城，进入房间还会掠夺玩家一定的金钱。每晚胜利后获得一些点数，用来开启随机的属性、技能等的选择界面。 [h1] 无中文[/h1] 游戏无中文，所以只简单玩了几局。没有中文还是很费事的，虽然英文并不难，但我英语也不行啊！实在懒得慢慢看，所以我玩的时候就基本没怎么看文本，包括技能效果、物品效果，都是靠简单扫描+实操摸个大概，所以可能导致个人体验有些主观武断。 [h1] 评价与印象[/h1] 1.本作最主要的游戏要素还是回合制战斗，而非地牢建设。 2.领主位置可以移动，而这个可以移动最大的意义，感觉还是早点和敌人战斗，防止敌人偷钱。同时还做出了棺材血量这种，如果你不移动，就根本不用管的限制。简单说，最省事的玩法还是老老实实呆着，等别人找你的棺材。 3.游戏似乎单一了一些，不同角色除了初始没啥变动，战斗也容易进入一种重复性工作的状态。 4.某种程度上，游戏的战斗成长机制，像是将能够自由加点与技能树学习的西幻RPG，将自由选择改为在预组好的分类中随机选择，虽然带有了肉鸽意味，增强了随机性，但减少了策略性与玩家自由培养角色的能力。（但实际不是同一类游戏，不能这么硬比，举个例子说说个人感觉而已） [h1] 总结[/h1] 《Few Nights More》是一款肉鸽类型的地下城防守游戏，虽然拥有着地牢建设的游戏要素，但游戏建筑机制并不有趣，主要玩法依旧是和敌人进行回合制的战斗。 总体质量不错，具有多名角色与地图，丰富的机制与系统，但我没有找到一个重复多次吸引我玩下去的点，尤其战斗本身并不rogue，比较容易公式化，重复性工作。 我觉得本身质量是ok的，不介意没有中文，并对这种类型感兴趣的玩家可以入手尝试。 [quote] 加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GHYX]干货游戏[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35106417/]我的鉴赏家[/url]，不定期为大家带来诚意满满的游戏体验干货。 [/quote]

An interesting rouge-like with much potential. Probably the most powerful endorsement is that it gives the "just one more turn/run" feeling. The tags and the store page give you a pretty good sense of what the game is about: you are a vampire defending their mansion from pesky human hunters. Every turn has two phases: manage your base/mansion/character and combat. Both phases have you plenty to do and there is enough randomization to keep every run interesting. However, the game needs quite a bit more work. The animation are few and choppy. There is some lore in the game, but it is not very much (needs more lore about the enemies) and it does not make much sense (that intro video is awful). There are balancing issues - once you know what you're doing and you have unlocked some meaningful upgrades, it is easy to steamroll the enemies. And worst of all, the base management UI is atrocious and needs an overhaul and/or many quality of life updates. Overall, I'd recommend this game, even in its current EA state. I've quite enjoyed the 18 hours or so I've put so far, and will likely put quite a few more hours.

In the current state of the game I cannot recommend buying for two main reasons. Reason 1: There are too many overlapping layers of RNG, which makes the game feel more like a game of roulette than a rougelike. Further explanation: The main way for your character to be able to progress is through its skills, and you get 2 predetermined basic skills to begin with. The main issue is additional skills are not only random, but some of the worst or most unusable skills seem to have a "drop weight" to them. And a lot of skills are niche (in that they only really work when combined with other skills). The other issue is not only do you need to RNG into the right combination of skills, but you also need to unlock skill slots in order to use said skills. How do you unlock them? Of course another layer of RNG, you can get a perk that MIGHT give you an option to unlock an additional skill slot. Reason 2: The balance is pretty bad. There are just too many balance issues which further makes the first reason above more frustrating. Another annoyance is there are too many skills/abilities that don't work on bosses and veterans, yet those are the enemies you'd want these things to work on. It's just a really bizarre design choice to have most of your enemies be bosses and veterans while you include abilities that don't work on them. Additionally, reloading the game will "reroll" choices you get, this is a known bug that is apparently getting patched. The issue here is that's the only reason I haven't already uninstalled this game. And you can end up going 10-20 reloads before getting ONE skill that fits a build you're going for. The dev said they are going to add a reroll system with a cost, but if you require that many rerolls to begin with, then there's a problem before that mechanic is even in the game. And let me be clear, skills and perks are not the only RNG element to the game. You have RNG with the following mechanics: acquiring rooms/traps/decor/trinkets/minions. Events are RNG. Skills/trinkets themselves (how they function) can often be RNG, the necromancers first basic skill is completely RNG. The Roguelike genre doesn't mean you make every mechanic a roll of the dice. Having "infinite" possibilities doesn't matter when you have to play for infinity to avoid frustration.

Great concept, horribly buggy and the general state it is in does NOT reflect the fact it's a full release. This feels like a hodgepodge EA-state of a game with a lot of growing pains that should not have survived beta. It runs badly at times, there are really weird technical bugs that reflect the makeshift nature behind a fairly good veneer of a game and the latest patch still has halloween decoration in it, while the release was end of january. Add to that, that they release two games almost back to back with a very similar design and premise and this feels like the forgotten proof of concept for their other game that is barely good enough to make them a few bucks. This is compounded by a very minute bunch of enemy types and actual strategies you can viably use. There's a broad variety of options here, each with the depth of a puddle, and often times, barely working. Overall balance is very meh right now from what I tried. Which is sad, because the game has a lot to offer, but right now, everything is way too shifty for me to recommend it. Unless this mess is getting in a few patches in the next months, I will not recommend it in good faith.

Tough to review this one as there's 95% of a great game here but the developers are no longer providing support. Basically they dropped the early access label and declared it complete despite it clearly needing work. Here's some examples that need fixing: The last update was Halloween so there's a number of Halloween reskin UI items and an event with a "Halloween buff" that doesn't seem to exist and the "?" next to doesn't provide a tool tip. The build number on the main menu is a "release candidate" Effect icons on characters are missing art and often descriptions, e.g. voidborn The invaders for the castle are indicated to come in different entrances, but you won't know the order or the speed that move at. The UI is locked to a certain aspect ratio and doesn't resize, I think you're 1080p or bust as far as I can tell. Lots of effects have "every X" nights but it isn't clear when they trigger. Not always clear which effects last just for the battle and which persist permantely On skill selection there's lots of "effects" that aren't explained. What does "enfold" do for example? Coffin HP max and regen isn't present on the UI and I can't find out how you would find out. During gameplay on cards it's not obvious what the impact of an effect is either. For extended endgame you need to merge an orb but if it's not equipped in slot 1,2 or 3 it's not detected so you get a game over. There's loads more but they should be fixable without too much effort. It's frustrating that this game is a couple of QoL/bug fix patches away from being a solid recommend but it doesn't look like it's happening.

[h1]Few Nights More - ★✮☆☆☆ [/h1] [i] Full review available on the [url=https://www.indieloupe.com/reviews/few-nights-more]IndieLoupe website.[/url] Review dated 04/02/2025.[/i] My first impressions upon opening [i]Few Nights More[/i] were not great. Despite being “released” - and I use the term loosely - this week, the game’s title screen welcomes new players with a Hallowe’en-themed skin, seemingly a three-month-old hangover from its time in early access. That the developers didn’t even put the effort into removing this (nor changing the game’s “You beat the final boss of Early Access" message) speaks volumes about their treatment of Few Nights More. The timing of its release, one day after their other game was dropped, also doesn’t inspire confidence. [i]Few Nights More[/i] doesn’t feel like a finished game - there’s so many parts of it that I still don’t properly understand, which I could never find an explanation for. It’s a confusing, unclear mess, with so many moving parts that balance effectively goes out of the window - every fight feels ridiculously easy right until the point that you’re hit with one that’s impossible. The sound effects are also perhaps the worst I’ve heard in a game. Rather than work on an idea and flesh it out, nothing seems to have had enough attention put into it. In trying to do too much, it comes out with less depth than if they’d taken one core mechanic and built upon it. Few Nights More is awarded ★✮☆☆☆ by IndieLoupe.com. What is this... I thought as I booted up the game. The sound effects were so loud I got annoyed and just quit. What is this... I thought as I started the game for a second time a few days later. This is so weird. I am not sure I like this... That session lasted over 6 hours and I was absolutely drained (hah) at the end of it... wow... This game is like a drug for me... I absolutely adore this game. So why a negative review? 0) It's finished. Devs say so. It may be finished but it is not complete. I fully understand the business realities. The game didn't do well enough so they moved on (I believe they replied something like that to another review don't quote me on it). I understand that. But I am neither one of the devs nor an investor. I am a player. A player who bought this late into EA. Sadly devs just kind of dropped it at the finish line with an unceremonious launch and a promise of an eventual patch. 1) What is this? You defend your castle in a turn-based strategy. 1) management phase where you buy, place, equip stuff, 2) map phase where you and your opponents move around said map and 3) battle phase where you battle against one group of enemies. Phases 2-3 alternate (chase a group on the map, then fight them, then chase another, fight them...). You pick your character/clan. Each clan has a different signature skill and unlockable passives. You pick your difficulty, castle (map) and school of magic (there are four and each allows for different playstyles). This provides a nice variety of approaches and stuff to upgrade (although it can make pacing a bit awkward as you are tempted to play more of the schools you already bought upgrades for/clans you have XP on instead of experimenting). 2) Features What is missing? Seemingly one castle (map layout) and a few heroes (honestly just skins/opposite sex and bits of lore for them). Not much. It is almost complete in that regard. The one thing I would add if I could would be randomised castles. Like each castle guarantees the number of rooms, perhaps dimensions of rooms, but their location changes. Right now I bought and upgraded three castles and I will play the one with most space for most rooms... probably forever... 3) Bugs Nothing major or game-breaking for me. But tons of small bugs. 4) Music Exceptional. Well done. Maybe a bit too reliant on moans for some tracks for my taste but I like it. 5) Art Thematic. I like it. I am really missing different death animations per cause of death. Everything feels weightless since it's the same every time. If the enemy got a heart attack when killed by terror or got torn to shreds if... well torn to shreds or if character sprites reflected health and buffs/debuffs it would be so much better. But I understand how much work that would be. 6) Sound design Basic. Lots of room for improvement here. 7) Story Intro and character and item descriptions. No story in game to tie it all up. 8) Quality of life Probably my greatest gripe with the game. Lots of information is scattered across different parts of UI (I want to see clan, lineage, and school info both on the map and during combat). Things are often unexplained or poorly explained (mostly skills, kind of a bummer in a game that's all about making decisions based on information). Missing tooltips in a lot of places (The most jarring is when given a special choice that changes stats and you can't see your stats...). Unneeded info (Showing one time effects on your personal lineage). UI is too damn small and unscalable (and game seems to ignore my attempts to change resolution and my eyes are bad...). This is not about more content just the presentation of what is there. Along with bugs I could make like a 100+ notes of what should be changed... 9) Conclusion Still I am enjoying my time despite all of that. A lot. So why a negative review? Because there are so many more polished games that are just more comfortable to play. As much as I want the devs to do well on their next projects this kind of soured me on their games. It's not a bad game. I just don't recommend it. Just that tad bit of polish, some fixes, and maybe add that fourth castle and complete the roster of characters and it swings into definitely buy this.

And on a third - if you're gonna have an achievement for reaching night 250 and effects that double or triple strength, pretty please do something when the number gets high enough to roll over a variable. Having something with a billion strength do 0 damage feels pretty bad.

It's a fine enough game I guess. There are a lot of weird design choices, though. Infinite Mode is really kind of meaningless, since it is just a series of battles - anything involving the different house mechanics (eg., minions, rooms, ranks) end up doing nothing. I'd recommend it, but I just ran into an enemy with more than 1 billion HP who was the only enemy fully immune to my build (literally is completely immune to Decay, the main mechanic of necromancer). I'm not really that happy with it. It's a fine enough game, but there are definitely better ways to spend your money. Get it on a sale.

I enjoyed the first 40 hours, so for most games that is good enough. But I liked this game so much I wanted to get all the achievements. Turns out that's literally impossible. The achievement to last 250 nights in infinity mode cannot be accomplished because of stack overflow errors. Boss HP's exceed the 32 bit signed integer value (roughly 2.1 billion) and then the game basically stops working. Things glitch out, the boss won't even spawn, your action points disappear. It's a mess. I cannot recommend this game until it fixes the stack overflow problem.

This game was able to entertain interesting mechanics and allowed you to really think up some interesting builds. I feel like if this game was appropriately optimized, it would be an insanely good rogue like, but unfortunately it fails to be honest with its own numbers. I have sunk around 43 hours into this game and just because of how it calculates its #'s, I can't 100% it without spending 45~ minutes a night for about 100 more nights. To clarify, this game is quite fun to play for it's standard mode, but infinity mode breaks in only unfun ways. Damage scaling doesn't work. Ability acquisition doesn't work. Trying to progress just doesn't work. I was on night 145~ on Nikolai for the darkness build, and cards from my spell book would just disappear at random, so if I wanted to have multiple copies of exhaust cards I'd just lose them. I started a pharalan necromancy run because of the power gain with gold per night and was at like 650+ power. But guess what? my abilities stopped increasing in actual damage since 300~ except for one ability. Because of all this power, I also got 100% multicast as per their legacy ability, but I couldn't even use multicast. It is supposed to be 5 max uses of multicast per ability per turn. But after I use the 5 for any ability, I only get one randomly. Many games may just crash when ur integers get too big, that is fun and normal. You know at that point that you have simply won the game. But here, the integers mean nothing, your choices mean nothing, and honestly your own enjoyment means nothing. You simply cannot build in any meaningful way as the game can't handle it. But yeah, until the innerworkings of this game that disable it from running properly fixed, I can never reccomend the infinity mode, and I can barely reccomend playing at all.

having beaten the game for the first time, I do not really know what to think about it. at first, it looked like a great game, but the more I play the less I feel like there really is. it could be because I picked the "Dark" faction which seems to be playing very differently from other factions (not having proper AP or skill assignments but rather drawing random skills and keeping 2 types of AP from every turn amongst other things) but in general, it is just...it is basically an early access title in the middle or the early stages of development. missing art, missing tutorialization/tutorials for things that are not applicable appearing (said dark faction not getting a proper explanation as an example), various issues with UI/control like being practically unable to assign decorations (which give bonuses) to rooms except for the "assign all" button, visual glitches during enemy attacks, numerous rooms being imensly powerful while other rooms are very weak, the distribution of prestige resources between the 4 factions without a reset button as well as no family bonuses for other families meaning you are encouraged to lock into only one specific style of play and to never change it up because your very limited prestige resource has been spent to unlock "dark" faction mechanics so your necromancer and blood faction have no upgrades at all, and playing the family of seducers all the other families (of which half need to be unlocked for prestige resources) do not have any kind of benefit (rogue legacy 2 did this well as an example by making every class accrue their own XP, which at every level treshold gives you either some % stats like intelligence or HP or gives you more carrying capacity, all of which applies no matter what character you pick - enocuraging you to play every class) with nothing to really do to truly define your run besides picking the room types and decor types, when you even the option to pick - usually you get random drops. merchants arrive at unknown times so you rarely know when you will even be able to spend your money, rooms need to be put in locations of appropriate size so a lot of of rooms just do not get a place to be put anywhere in the first place, and you only really care about their main and leveled up bonuses - meaning you probably will pick any room that gives prestige/terror/seduction per night and almost everything else is just useless for the most part. it...it really just feels like someone was on the path of making something great or at least OK, but from what I can tell nothing more will come. I for some reason have the "valentine event" visible on my main menu, telling me everone starts wtih like 30 or 40 extra seduction - even before I knew what it was (just like terror and prestige, (not to be confused with prestige resources), it is something that fills up a bar which gets you specific bonuses at specific tresholds), and it does not even seem to apply despite being visible on the screen. rerolling skills seems to not cost anything? if so, why would I not just reroll forever? I think I am rambling at this point. just...be aware that when you stop playing this game, you will be wishing for more; not because the game is over and you still crave it, but because it offers you a promise it cannot deliver on and now you just want something that will

This should still be in early access, big dawg. It's 90% of the way there, but that 10% is not coming and it's a pretty crucial 10%. Stuff that's missing: Bugfixes (my first issue was ten minutes in when I allocated fame from my living room and it just disappeared... for ten nights before randomly applying itself) Tooltips (they're there on some stuff, but missing from a lot of other stuff, and this is a game that kinda requires you to know how stuff works) UI (buttons you press inside a window during your administration phase are also pressed outside that window. Also how do you merge orbs? Also nothing ever works more than like 60% intuitively or explains why it's doing this. I think your first two skills are unremovable from your build, but the game doesn't tell you this and also what? Why?) Variety (portraits look nice and I seriously appreciate the time taken to hand draw everything, but also you can swap the gender on your first four lords but not your second four, and for one of them that looks fine but for the others it feels strongly like cut content) Bugs again (the music turned off about thirty minutes into my run and would not turn back on, it also loops and switches tracks badly, also SFX are tuned like 500% above where they need to be on default settings good god) The core game is a dungeon keeper esque darkest dungeon esque thing where you're expected to grind multiple loops in order to have enough points invested in a character so that they can handle mid and late game bosses. I genuinely don't think you can win this one on your first run, which I don't mind, but might put some people off. It has a lot of heart, and if it was still in early access or there was any plan to continue development, I'd be cutting it more slack. There's good bones here, it's just that some of the meat is hanging off of them and the whole thing is kinda shambling around in a tormented halflife. Edit: In case it adds more credence to any of what I've said here, it's 2026. The valentine's event from 2025 (which unbalanced the game by starting you with 30 in one of your prestige tracks) is still running. And also because this thing is buggy the event does not actually provide the 30 in your prestige track that it promises. It's just there and provides nothing.

As far as the game systems go, this thing is a blast. Lot's of variety and replayability. The downside is that it's very janky, unpolished, and buggy. Descriptions are missing, the UI is just bad... But I'm still having fun playing it.

I really like this game (just look at the amount of hours played) and overall I would recommend it, especially for the price they ask for it. The good: Because of the different disciplines, the different vampire clans and the numerous random generated aspects, no run will ever be the same. Which I personally love. For every run you're awarded points that you can spend to strengthen the disciplines or buy general bonusses. Beside this each character will gain experience, which will grant unique aspects of that clan. And speaking about clans, they are different enough to really impact your run. (some are more unique than others) The bad: The main negative aspect in my opinion is that this game feels like it still should be in early access, because there are still numerous bugs, glitches, balance issues and seemingly unreleased content, but it really seems that the developers have completely stopped working on this game. Most bugs are minor, like glitching background music, overlapping texts, disproportionate sound effects, stuch descriptions, UI bugs, missing aspects with loading saved games, etc. But there are also quite big issues. If you for instance like to 100% a game with its achievements, forget it. In endless mode past night 200 the game will have scaled to such high numbers that the game itself can't handle it. Overall with what you get for this price, I really think it does deserve a positive recommendation, but the fact that the developers seemingly just have abandoned this game in its current state, really reflect badly on them. And it's such a shame because I do believe that with a bit more attention and love, this game could easily go from decent to great...
画风好看，玩法丰富， 新人建议第二个人物开局，选第二个承诺，召唤流开局，围绕召唤仆人+陷阱发展，对面boss见面都是大残；提前注意小兵的出兵顺序，可以实现收益最大化； 局外养成前面8小时比较慢，建议多死多刷，不要太计较选什么技能和流派，因为你大概率会被某个boss秒掉，通过前期速刷，把局外等级养起来，随便爽。

游戏的底子（整体框架）非常不错，玩家作为吸血鬼领主在上一次战争中被封印，此次地狱归来，与正义（？）势力再次决一死战，在每一夜中可以获得属性、技能、房间、装备、仆从、陷阱等等物品提升自己，面对难度逐步提高的挑战。内容很丰富，8名不同的角色，四种不同的流派，每种流派至少有十几种技能和对应的装备，还可以用房间来建造城堡，装备还有着一些合成公式，看似内容相当丰富，实则槽点不少。 各方面都有一些略显粗糙的点，首先不得不提的是翻译，很像机翻而且还有一些内容没翻译完我真的没绷住。游戏共有两个模式，经典和无尽，经典模式就是活过18夜就算胜利，如果你用三个秘密宝珠合成了终极宝珠在18夜时佩戴在身上可以解锁隐藏的第四章19，20，21夜，这看似是个很好的设计，但是隐藏的3夜及其粗糙，就是把以前的敌人成批出现，仅此而已，比如第21夜的敌人是两个17夜的boss+18夜的boss，就这样，没什么新的内容，只有在第一次解锁隐藏关时有那么一丝期待，给我的感觉是诚意不足，既然都考虑到了隐藏为什么不做好点，哦对了，用来合成解锁隐藏关道具的宝石，需要在游戏中击败别的吸血鬼领主获得，有种击败与你同一时间竞争的玩家的感觉，设定上做的不错，但是隐藏关却没什么新内容，令人唏嘘。 在经典模式通关（打完最终boss）后，游戏的报幕阶段显示的是“恭喜您已击败测试版本的最终boss”，但是我去steam主页一看并不是测试版，这就是正式版，且在血液再临之后开发商还有在开发别的游戏，好吧，看来好像是被制作组放弃了。 再说无尽模式，无尽模式更是敷衍，我本来以为无尽模式就是经典模式的变种，到18/21夜不结束，但无尽模式没有城堡，没有房间建造，没有仆从、陷阱，只有纯粹的战斗，内容压缩得更为贫瘠，只玩了一次我就心生退意。 作为一个有着rogue要素齐全的游戏，局外成长有点多，两千点数为上限，在我点了一千点左右的时候，用一个没玩过的角色打基础难度，已经输不掉了，局外能成长的东西有点多，角色的技能、能选的城堡、开局自带两房间等等确实是有点多，而且有很大助力，但看在不同游戏难度的强度区别很大的份上倒也合理。 值得一提的是，作为一个roguelite游戏，是可以选择难度的，类比杀戮尖塔的进阶0到进阶20，本游戏的难度叫“辐射”，一看到这个词我就想到了吸血鬼对阳光的惧怕，这倒是挺有意思的。有些局外成长内容需要通过高难度（比如辐射8），离谱的来了，血液再临允许跨难度挑战，比如我刚打过辐射1，这次直接打辐射8，通过了，成就也跳了，但是那个局外成长内容点不了，重新选角色，推荐的是辐射3，也就是相当于你刚才打过的是辐射2，当时我确实有点顶不住了，允许跨难度挑战，却不能跨难度解锁，我还试了好几遍，最高难度都打了，还是不能解锁，玩到这里我就觉得差不多到此为止吧。 刚开始玩的10h非常有趣，内容看似丰富，但是既完成度不够又粗糙，欠缺打磨，明明设置了十几个难度和需要一定时间游玩解锁的局外内容，游戏的内容却完全撑不起这些时长。
